c.tagline: Brazil's island capital of 42 beaches, lagoons and surf.

taxi.fareNote: City taxis are metered; ride-hailing apps like Uber and 99 are usually cheaper than street taxis.

emergency.note: 190 reaches the military police, 192 summons a SAMU ambulance, and 193 reaches the fire brigade.

avoid.reason: Avoid the mainland periphery favelas such as Monte Cristo — gang activity, with no tourist sights there.
Watch phones and bags on busy beaches and around the Centro bus terminal (TICEN) after dark.

hood_desc: The historic downtown on the mainland-facing side of Santa Catarina Island, home to the colonial Public Market, the cathedral and the landmark Hercílio Luz Bridge; the walkable, transit-hub base for first-timers who want city services over beach life.

The island's buzziest district, wrapped around a large saltwater lagoon and packed with restaurants, bars, organic markets and nightlife, plus a launch point for surfing, sandboarding and stand-up paddle; popular with expats and younger travelers.
An upscale planned beach neighborhood on the calm north shore, known for mansions, clear water and glamorous summer beach clubs; suits travelers wanting polished resort comfort and a party scene.
A busy family-oriented north-shore beach resort area with gentle warm water, plenty of pousadas and a strong Argentine tourist presence in summer; good for a relaxed beach holiday.
A laid-back, bohemian beach district on the east coast with a long surf beach and access to Campeche Island; suits surfers and those wanting a mellow, nature-close pace.

water.note: Tap is treated, but most locals drink filtered or bottled.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 5am to midnight; there is no metro or rail, so late-night travel relies on taxis and ride-hailing apps.
transit.note: Florianópolis has no metro or train — the island runs on an integrated municipal bus network (SETUF, operated by Consórcio Fênix) built around hub terminals (TICEN downtown plus TIRIO, TILAG, TISAN and others), with three road bridges linking Santa Catarina Island to the mainland.
transit.pay: Pay cash to the driver or tap a rechargeable Cartão Bus card; a single fare is about R$5.30, with free transfers inside the integrated terminals.

sys.n: SETUF integrated municipal bus network (Consórcio Fênix)

tip.r: A 10% service charge is usually already added to restaurant bills; extra tipping is optional.

landmarks: Hercílio Luz Bridge
Brazil's longest suspension bridge and the city's glowing steel icon, linking Santa Catarina Island to the mainland since 1926.
Lagoa da Conceição
The island's vibrant heart, a saltwater lagoon ringed by dunes, seafood restaurants and viewpoints, buzzing with windsurfers and nightlife.
Praia da Joaquina and the Dunes
A legendary surf beach backed by vast white dunes where locals sandboard down slopes overlooking the Atlantic.
Ilha do Campeche
A protected offshore island of Caribbean-clear water and ancient rock inscriptions, reached by boat from Campeche or Armação beaches.
Mercado Público de Florianópolis
The ochre-colored 19th-century public market downtown, where stalls of fresh seafood surround bars famous for pastel de camarão and cold beer.
Santo Antônio de Lisboa
A charming Azorean fishing village of whitewashed colonial houses, oyster farms and sunset views across the bay to the mainland.
Fortaleza de São José da Ponta Grossa
A restored 18th-century Portuguese fortress between Jurerê and Daniela beaches, its whitewashed batteries guarding the island's northern strait.
Praia Mole
A gorgeous surf-and-see-and-be-seen beach framed by green headlands, hosting international surf and bodyboard competitions.
Ribeirão da Ilha
The island's oldest Azorean settlement, a waterfront strip of pastel houses and terraces serving oysters pulled straight from the calm bay.
Morro da Cruz Viewpoint
The 285-meter city summit delivering 360-degree panoramas over downtown, the bridges and both bays, especially dazzling at night.

train.note: Brazil has no intercity passenger trains, and Santa Catarina has no passenger railway at all. Travel to and from Florianópolis is by coach, car or plane.

intl.to: Buenos Aires (Argentina) & Montevideo (Uruguay) - seasonal summer services
intl.op: JBL Turismo / Crucero del Norte — tickets at the Rita Maria terminal

bus.note: The Rodoviária Rita Maria sits at the island end of the bridges, walkable from the centre. Catarinense, Santo Anjo and Reunidas run constantly to Curitiba (about 5 hours), São Paulo (11) and Porto Alegre (6); book through ClickBus (https://www.clickbus.com.br/) or Buser (https://www.buser.com.br/). The Argentine and Uruguayan coaches are mostly a summer holiday trade - carry your passport and expect long border stops.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry - Florianópolis sits on an island but is joined to the mainland by road bridges. Small boats run out to Ilha do Campeche and along the Ribeirão da Ilha as excursions, and the schooner trips around the bay are sightseeing rather than transport.

full.name: São Francisco do Sul
